scores.claim_text: Air Products is the primary beneficiary of NEOM Green Hydrogen Company (NGHC), constructing green-hydrogen-to-ammonia facility in NEOM City with ACWA Power and NEOM Company; APD is exclusive offtaker under long-term take-if-tendered agreement; ~$6.1B project financing (~73% of project); ~$0.8B EPC performance guarantee; onstream 2027.
supports: edgar_fts NEOM Green Hydrogen: 44 hits across EDGAR including APD 10-Ks/10-Qs/8-Ks; multiple 8-K announcements going back to 2021/2023 corroborate construction progress and project narrative continuity.
edgar_fts ACWA Power: 65 hits; recurring APD 8-K disclosures (Oct-2021, Jan-2023, May-2023) align with disclosed joint-venture partnership.
scores.interpretation: Highly verifiable, well-disclosed mega-project. APD itself is the exclusive offtaker, so the Rule-7 third-party-counterparty-disclosure test does NOT apply. Heuristic 3 (planned-vs-operational): the project is honestly described as UNDER CONSTRUCTION with onstream target 2027 (still ~12-18 months post-cutoff). APD's own risk factors explicitly flag that 'our large-scale clean hydrogen projects are being built before finalization of offtake agreements for a substantial percentage of expected production' - high transparency, no headline-capacity conflation. $6.1B non-recourse project financing, $0.8B EPC performance guarantee (declining, expiring Nov 2028). PASS.

scores.claim_text: FY2025 charges of ~$3.7B pre-tax for business and asset actions (~$3.6B project-exit costs primarily related to clean energy generation and distribution projects); operating loss of $877M vs. operating income of $4.5B in FY2024.
supports: edgar_fts 'project exit' restricted to APD CIK: 15 hits across consecutive quarterly filings (Q2-FY2025 8-K, Q2/Q3/Q4 FY2025 10-Qs, FY2025 10-K, FY2026 Q1 and Q2 10-Qs) - confirms recurring, multi-quarter exit narrative.
scores.M_value: 15 hits in APD's own filings spanning fiscal-year 2025 and into fiscal-year 2026
scores.interpretation: This is APD's own admission that previously announced clean-energy projects did not pass return thresholds and were cancelled/descoped. By the EXTRACT RUBRIC this is a high-discriminative financial-distress-adjacent claim; by Calibration Heuristic 3 it is essentially the company conceding that the prior 'announced GW' marketing tier exceeded what could be delivered economically. APD's transparency about the magnitude ($3.7B charge, single-year operating loss) is appropriate. Read as a forward signal: announced-vs-operational gap was real for several legacy projects; remaining hydrogen pipeline (NEOM, Louisiana, Alberta) should be monitored under the same stage ladder. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY rather than SEVERE because (a) the new CEO and board explicitly disclosed and quantified the exit, and (b) the surviving projects (NEOM in particular) have separately-confirmed third-party project finance and partner equity.

scores.claim_text: APD exited the World Energy SAF expansion project (Paramount, CA); recorded $300M credit-loss allowance on the World Energy financing receivable and wrote off $329.4M of deferred project costs.
supports: edgar_fts 'World Energy' restricted to APD CIK: 14 hits including 8-K filed 2025-02-24 (the exit announcement window) plus 10-Qs in FY2024-FY2025 - corroborates the in-and-out narrative.
scores.interpretation: World Energy SAF expansion was acquired Nov-2023, exited 2025 - a ~$629M loss event ($300M reserve + $329.4M deferred-cost writedown) on a roughly 16-month timeline. This is the clearest example in the filing of the announced-vs-delivered gap at APD. The exit was permit-driven (project 'put on hold pending receipt of permits'), which is a recognised stage-ladder slip from FID to construction. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: APD disclosed clearly, fully reserved, and stated 'no further loss exposure' but the underlying signal is that APD took asset-impairment in a specific named clean-energy bet inside two years of acquisition. Reinforces the C2 read.

scores.claim_text: APD invested ~$7.0B in additions to plant and equipment in FY2025 supporting clean energy initiatives including NEOM, Louisiana clean energy complex, and Alberta clean energy complex; FY2026 capex guidance ~$4B.
supports: epa_frs Air Products in Louisiana: 33 EPA-regulated facilities including 'AIR PRODUCTS REG H2 PIPELINE' in Geismar (Ascension Parish, on Gulf Coast hydrogen pipeline) and merchant/distribution sites in Sulphur, Baton Rouge, etc.
epa_frs Air Products in Texas: 26 facilities (Beaumont etc) confirming the disclosed Gulf Coast pipeline footprint.
scores.M_check: epa_frs.query_facilities(Air Products, LA) and (Air Products, TX)
scores.M_value: 33 LA facilities, 26 TX facilities; named H2 pipeline in Geismar LA on EPA registry
scores.interpretation: EPA FRS independently confirms APD's Gulf Coast hydrogen pipeline footprint at the substring level. The Louisiana clean energy complex (blue hydrogen) sits on top of an already-operating, EPA-permitted footprint in the same parishes - low fabrication risk. PASS on the named-facility component of the claim. Note: 'announced' vs 'operating' status of the new clean-energy build remains a stage-ladder watch item (Heuristic 3) but the underlying physical-asset claim is corroborated.

scores.claim_text: JIGPC joint venture with Saudi Aramco Power Company, ACWA Power, and APQ supplies electricity, steam, hydrogen and utilities to Aramco's Jazan refinery/terminal complex under 25-year agreement, commenced; APD invested $115M final equity in FY2025; ME&I segment equity-affiliates income $340.9M FY2025.
supports: edgar_fts 'Jazan': 138 hits across EDGAR including multiple APD 8-Ks (Nov-2019, Oct-2021, Jan-2023) - independent press-release and refinery-operator corroboration of Jazan project linkage.
scores.interpretation: JIGPC is in operation (25-year supply agreement commenced, recurring equity income of ~$340M/yr from ME&I segment). Multi-filer EDGAR corroboration plus APD's recurring 8-K press releases. PASS. This is the kind of operating, contracted long-term industrial-gas relationship that the Calibration Heuristic 4 (investment-vs-operating distinction) treats as the real-revenue end-state.

scores.claim_text: BHIG (Blue Hydrogen Industrial Gases Company) was deconsolidated in Jan-2025 when APQ issued equity to Saudi Aramco Development Company creating a 50/50 JV; ~$675M of long-term debt derecognized; BHIG constructing plants and pipelines in Jubail Industrial City, Saudi Arabia; $238M FY2025 advances to BHIG.
supports: edgar_fts 'Jubail': 161 hits across EDGAR (multi-filer; Phillips 66, others discuss Saudi industrial gas footprint at Jubail) - confirms Jubail Industrial City is a known counterparty geography.
scores.interpretation: Deconsolidation arithmetic is internally consistent ($675M debt derecognition + segment-operating-income improvement called out specifically by the company). Heuristic 4 applies: this is an investment / equity restructuring at the JV level, not a new commercial revenue claim. PASS.

scores.claim_text: APD owns a large patent portfolio in hydrogen / electrolyzer / industrial-gas technology with active R&D in US, UK, and Saudi Arabia.
supports: uspto_odp Air Products and Chemicals: 766 total applications, 329 granted patents pre-cutoff. Category counts: 102 hydrogen-area (hydrogen/electrolyz/fuel cell/ammonia/SMR/reformer/gasif), 47 cryogenic, 351 other. Recent applications include 'Hydrogen-Enhanced Pulverized Coal Ignition', 'Hydrogen Gas Output from a Trailer', etc.
scores.M_value: 329 granted patents; 102 hydrogen-area hits; 47 cryogenic hits
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 8 threshold: PASS when n_granted >= 10 with claimed-area hit. APD has 329 granted patents with 102 hydrogen-area hits - more than 30x the minimum. No Nikola pattern (granted-but-zero-in-area). PASS with high confidence.

scores.claim_text: APD operates a large EPA-regulated US industrial-gas footprint including Gulf Coast / California / Arizona pipeline systems and ~445 Americas production/distribution facilities; Americas segment sales $5,125.9M FY2025.
supports: epa_frs Air Products in CA: 71 EPA-registered facilities (multiple in Carson, LA, etc).
epa_frs Air Products in TX: 26 facilities.
epa_frs Air Products in LA: 33 facilities including named H2 pipeline assets in Geismar.
scores.M_value: 71 + 26 + 33 = 130 EPA-registered APD facilities in three core US states alone
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 1 (EPA FRS scope): industrial gas H2 production plants ARE EPA-regulated. APD has overwhelming registry presence across the named pipeline geographies (Gulf Coast / California) - the physical-facility component of the claim is heavily corroborated. PASS.
